title: The Lighthouse Cat's Last Shift
sources: Original fiction written for this episode (marked "fiction": true). Inspired by the documented tradition of lighthouse-keeping cats, e.g. Tibs, the Post Office cat, and the lighthouse cats recorded by the National Lighthouse Museum — no specific real cat's story is retold.

lines.text: For thirty-one years, a cat named Biscuit kept the lighthouse burning.
lines.caps: For thirty-one | years, | a cat named | Biscuit kept | the lighthouse | burning.

lines.text: Every night at dusk, she climbed the ninety-nine iron steps alone,
lines.caps: Every night | at dusk, she | climbed the | ninety-nine iron | steps alone,

lines.text: she trimmed the wick, she polished the great glass lens,
lines.caps: she trimmed | the wick, she | polished the great | glass lens,

lines.text: and she watched the fog roll in like a slow grey sea.
lines.caps: and she watched | the fog roll | in like a | slow grey sea.

lines.text: Then one October night, the supply boat never came.
lines.caps: Then one | October night, | the supply boat | never came.

lines.text: The oil ran low, the wind rose, and a fishing boat was lost in the dark.
lines.caps: The oil | ran low, the | wind rose, and | a fishing boat | was lost in | the dark.

lines.text: So Biscuit did the one thing no keeper had ever taught her.
lines.caps: So Biscuit did | the one thing | no keeper had | ever taught her.

lines.text: She dragged the spare oil up, one small can at a time,
lines.caps: She dragged the | spare oil up, | one small can | at a time,

lines.text: And at dawn, Biscuit finally slept, the lighthouse still burning.
lines.caps: And at dawn, | Biscuit finally | slept, | the lighthouse | still burning.
